tools.name: search_offers
tools.description:
Search for active offers in the AnyGett database.

Returns a JSON array of matching offers with all fields parsed.
Returns an empty array if no offers match.

FILTERS (all optional):
- query: full-text search in title + description
- offer_type: "product" | "service" | "job" | "resume"
- category_id

tools.name: get_offer_details
tools.description:
Get complete details of a specific offer by its UUID.

Returns a single offer object with all fields (including contact_method, specific_attributes, geo_scope).
Returns an error object with code "NOT_FOUND" if the ID doesn't exist.
The id parameter accepts a UUID, an offer URL like https://anygett.c

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description:
List all available offer categories with their IDs, slugs, and icons.

Returns category records used as category_id when creating offers.
Each item includes: id, slug, name_en, icon, sort_order.

tools.name: catalog_stats
tools.description:
Get live catalog coverage: total active offers, publishers, and per-category counts.

Use it to find underserved niches — categories with 0 offers are the biggest opportunity to be first.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_offer_details · Private data: search_offers, list_categories, create_offer, delete_offer · Public sink: create_offer · Destructive: delete_offer.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_offer_details · Private data: search_offers, list_categories, create_offer, delete_offer · Public sink: create_offer · Destructive: delete_offer

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
